title: Signed-span-envelope connector for 3rd-party Tempo gateway
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a connector that accepts vendor-issued, signed span envelopes (compact envelope format with per-tenant signatures) and reliably converts them into our internal OTLP-compatible span stream for Tempo ingestion. Several enterprise customers ingest spans from a certified partner that signs payloads using ECDSA/ED25519 and expects us to verify signatures, enforce replay protection, and forward validated spans to Tempo with minimal added latency and clear operational metrics. The connector must support key rotation (partner publishes public keys), pluggable crypto verification, idempotent ingestion to avoid duplicate billing/alerts, per-tenant mapping, and surge buffering/backpressure so spikes don't drop customer data. This ticket covers design, implementation plan, tests, dashboards, rollout strategy, and a staged canary to Dedicated clusters before Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Connector accepts signed envelope POSTs on /v1/signed-spans with H/JSON envelope (RFC style) and returns 202 on valid verification
Signature verification implemented with pluggable algorithms (initially ECDSA-secp256k1 + ED25519) and integrated with KMS-backed public key rotation
Idempotency/deduplication ensures duplicate envelopes within configured window are not double-forwarded to Tempo
Per-tenant mapping and rate limits are applied and exposed in metrics and logs
End-to-end latency from received envelope to Tempo write acknowledged < 2s p50 under normal load, SLO defined and measured
Comprehensive unit/integration tests and a canary deployment plan documented with rollback criteria
tasks: Draft RFC for envelope format and verification API (confluence link below)
Implement envelope HTTP endpoint + parsing and validation
Integrate crypto verification libraries and KMS for public key rotation
Build idempotency store (Redis with 24h TTL) and dedupe logic
Translate envelope to OTLP spans, preserve original trace/span ids and attributes
Implement buffering queue with priority lanes per-tenant and backpressure hooks
Add metrics and tracing for verification latency, failures, dedupe rate, queue depth
Write unit and integration tests (including tampered-signature cases and rotated-key scenarios)
Create dashboard panels (errors, verification latency, queueing, per-tenant throughput)
Prepare canary rollout runbook, impact analysis, and run the canary on Dedicated cluster
Document API for partners and internal runbook for key rotation and incident handling
design_notes: Envelope schema: compact JSON with fields: tenant_id, algorithm, key_id, signature, payload_base64, timestamp, idempotency_key (optional)
Verification flow: fetch public key from KMS cache; try key_id first; fallback to key discovery endpoint for rotated keys
Idempotency strategy: prefer explicit idempotency_key when provided; otherwise use SHA256(payload || key_id) as derived key
Dedup window: default 24h, configurable per-tenant. Store keys with TTL in Redis cluster with high availability
Ordering: we cannot strictly order across tenants; preserve per-trace ordering by buffering spans belonging to same trace id and forwarding sequentially when possible
Batching: translate to OTLP batches sized for current throughput and Tempo recommended max batch size; avoid creating large batches that increase tail latency
Backpressure: if Tempo write latency spikes or queue saturation occurs, start shedding non-critical low-sampling-rate traces and surface metrics
Security: verify signatures before any parsing to avoid resource exhaustion attacks. Rate limit verification attempts per source IP and tenant
Audit logging: log verification failures with non-sensitive metadata to support partner debugging and security reviews
decisions: Initial algorithms supported: ED25519 and ECDSA-secp256k1. Rationale: partner ecosystem support and hardware acceleration availability
Use Redis cluster for idempotency store to keep implementation simple and leverage existing infra
Expose key rotation endpoints and cache keys for 5m; fetch fallback on verification failure
Return 202 Accepted for valid envelopes to decouple verification+forwarding from client latency. Provide a status API for partners to poll forwarding state
Implement per-tenant configurable dedupe and surge policies via Redwood Console settings (deferred to separate UI ticket)
risks: Signature verification can become CPU-heavy at high throughput; may need crypto offload or batching of verification requests
Idempotency store size could grow with high-cardinality tenants; requires monitoring and eviction policy tuning
Incorrect mapping of tenant ids or replay protection gaps could cause data leakage or duplicate billing
Backpressure heuristics might lead to unexpected shedding of important low-volume traces if thresholds are misconfigured
